annotator_prompt.name: selected_placement
annotator_prompt.description: The failures occurred when the requested placement was correctly identified, but purple targets subsequently exchanged positions near the end of the demonstration. A single release image identified the target's old position, so the policy transferred toward that position rather than the same target's final position. This breaks SUFFICIENCY: target identity after the exchange cannot be recovered from the release image and execution scene alone. Change this field to an ordered list of demonstration keyframes documenting the selected target's identity through any subsequent target motion. The first entry remains the earliest identifiable completed release for the requested ordinal. Follow that physical target through the rest of the demonstration. If it subsequently moves, append the last shown frame before each motion interval, every shown frame during that interval, and the first shown frame establishing its settled destination. Do not duplicate labels. If it does not subsequently move, retain a one-element list. Determine correspondence by continuous motion, not by nearest final location or spatial rank. Fill this list at the video cycle and retain it unchanged during execution. For example, a first release identified at V192 followed by an exchange late in the video requires a list beginning with V192 and including the exchange frames, rather than V192 alone. Preserve the chronological release-counting rule; do not relabel a later placement as the requested one.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: selected_placement
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: A correctly selected release image can become insufficient when identical purple targets exchange positions later in the video. Saving only that image loses the physical target's identity at execution and breaks SUFFICIENCY. During the video cycle, count completed releases of the instructed cube as before and identify the requested target. Then inspect the remainder of the available video and track that target continuously, including target motion after the cube has been returned to bare table. Write an ordered list whose first entry is the earliest identifiable release frame. If the selected target later moves, append the last shown frame before each motion interval, every shown frame during it, and the first shown frame establishing its settled destination, without duplicate labels. Use surrounding video frames to establish that motion has ended. If the selected target never moves afterward, write only the release label in a one-element list, for example ["V464"]. A moving-target example starts with ["V192", ...] and includes the later exchange frames. On act cycles copy the entire incoming list unchanged. Do not substitute a different placement or infer identity from the target's final spatial rank.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: The failed transfers followed the selected target's placement-time position even though targets had exchanged positions later in the demonstration. This breaks SUFFICIENCY under the old static matching rule. Replace the instruction to match the ring supporting the cube directly to the current layout with this rule: identify the selected physical ring in the first retained frame, follow its continuous motion through the remaining retained frames, and match its settled destination to the current scene. The requested ordinal identifies a placement event, not a fixed tabletop location. Use the selected ring's current center for transfer, descent, and retreat. When there are no later motion frames, direct matching from the release image still applies. Keep the calibrated projection, pickup, lift, arrival-tolerance, release, and retreat rules unchanged; do not reproduce the demonstration's button presses or target exchanges.
proposal.refused: The reports correctly exposed a mismatch between placement-time locations and recorded destinations, but their suggested remedies of selecting another release image or changing calibration are not supported. The full demonstrations show late target exchanges: the blue cube's third-placement ring moves from the lower-left location to the upper-left location, and its first-placement ring in another demonstration moves from the image-right middle location to the image-left location. The original release selections therefore remain correct; their later motion was what memory omitted. In particular, the claim that the lower-left ring's old image position projects to approximately x=-0.002 rather than x=0.14 is false. Those coordinates describe different positions before and after the exchange, not a calibration correction. Once identity is tracked through the exchange, the existing hover-arrival rule already calls for descent when the hand is over the recorded destination. No special arrival exception or episode-specific coordinate override should be added.

texts.action:
At the video cycle output memory only. Execution begins with the gripper open above the table. Use selected_placement to identify the destination physical purple ring. Identify the ring supporting the instructed cube in the first retained frame, then follow that ring's continuous motion through the remaining retained frames to its settled destination. Match that destination to the current scene using the fixed camera and surrounding target layout. If the list contains only the release frame, match directly from that frame. The requested ordinal identifies a placement event and its physical ring, not a fixed tabletop location or the cube's final demonstration location. Use the selected ring's current center for transfer, descent, and retreat. Do not reproduce the demonstration's target exchanges. Do not reproduce the demonstration's button press or its other placements. Manipulate only the instructed color.

Estimate world positions with the calibrated cameras rather than image left/right guesses. Intersect target-center rays with the tabletop plane z=0. Estimate cube horizontal center using its top face at approximately z=0.04, or its footprint at table height; do not project an elevated cube center onto the tabletop. Use the wrist view to refine alignment. World +y is image right in the front camera. Set the hand vertically downward, roll pi (equivalently -pi), pitch zero, and choose yaw aligned with the cube's horizontal edges, choosing the equivalent grasp angle nearest zero. Preserve this grasp orientation while carrying and releasing.

Apply these state-dependent rules. With an open hand and the instructed cube resting away from its destination, if the hand is not already at a pickup hover, command the cube's horizontal center at z=0.15 with gripper open. If the open hand is at that hover, within approximately 1.5 cm horizontally and 1 cm vertically, descend to the visually estimated cube center at z=0.02 and close the gripper. Correct horizontal alignment from the images rather than treating the reported TCP position as the exact previous command.

With the cube held between closed fingers near table height, lift vertically over its current horizontal center to z=0.15, keeping closed. Do not transfer sideways before lifting. With the held cube at z approximately 0.15 and not over the selected target, command the selected target center at z=0.15, keeping closed. With the held cube at hover height over that target, descend to the target center at z=0.005 and open. Treat the usual several-millimetre tracking error as arrival; do not insert unnecessary correction waypoints. With the hand open near the target and the cube released there, retract to the same target center at z=0.15 with the gripper open. This retreat applies even when the wrist or fingers partially obscure the resting cube; use the visible ring, open fingers, and current motion frames to recognize the release.

If perception is ambiguous, use the retained placement and target-motion frames together with both current views to resolve the selected ring's identity and current position before moving toward it. If the cube was not grasped, apply the open-hand pickup rules again using its observed location. If no rule is applicable because the hand occludes the relevant objects, move vertically to a clear z=0.15 observation pose, preserving the gripper state and any held cube, then reassess. Never guess a different target from its ordinal's spatial rank. Do not wait without a visible settling-related purpose, and never command a waypoint identical to the current TCP; any necessary gripper-only change must include at least 2 mm of safe motion.
